exercise.name: Dumbbell Incline One Arm Lateral Raise

reference.title: Dumbbell Incline One Arm Lateral Raise
reference.listing: Page not read (gymvisual.com is blocked by the proxy); movement taken from the exercise name and standard coaching practice.
reference.note: Reference used only to identify the movement. No GymVisual media is stored here; this rig, model and animation are original.

breathing.pattern: Breathe out as the arm rises, breathe in as it lowers.
breathing.cadence: About 1.5 s up, short pause, about 2 s down

prescription.load: Light dumbbell; the side-lying angle loads the bottom of the raise

cues.text: Turn an incline bench (about 45 degrees) across your path. Sit side-on on the seat, lean your left side on the pad with the left arm hooked over its top, feet on the floor. The right arm starts angled down across the front of the body, thumb forward.
Breathe out and raise the straight arm out and up, leading with the elbow, until it is just past vertical to the floor.
Pause with the arm about straight up; no shrug.
Breathe in and lower slowly back down across the body.
Keep a little tension at the bottom and repeat. Then switch sides.

mistakes.mistake: Rolling the body away from the pad to lift
mistakes.fix: Keep the left side on the pad; only the arm moves.

mistakes.mistake: Shrugging the shoulder to the ear
mistakes.fix: Keep the shoulder down; lead with the elbow.

mistakes.mistake: Bending the elbow more as you lift

kinematics.norm: From the arm across the front of the body up to about vertical to the floor (clinical opinion); lying on an incline shifts the hardest part of the raise toward the start (Coratella 2020 compared lateral raise variations)
Pad about 45 degrees, the left side of the ribs resting on it, the bottom arm over the top edge (clinical opinion)
Side-on to the pad, still (clinical opinion)

sources.title: GymVisual #1368, Dumbbell Incline One Arm Lateral Raise, video (movement reference only; page not read)
Coratella et al. 2020, an electromyographic analysis of lateral raise variations and frontal raise in competitive bodybuilders (Int J Environ Res Public Health 17(17):6015)
Campos et al. 2020, different shoulder exercises affect the activation of deltoid portions in resistance-trained individuals (J Hum Kinet 75:5-14)

cautions: Stop if sharp pain, a pinching feeling in the front or top of the shoulder, numbness or tingling occurs.
The dumbbell load is user-chosen: pick a weight you can control for every rep with good form.
Muscle glow colours and activation curves are illustrative, not measured EMG.
Stop if it pinches at the top of the shoulder; raise a little lower.
modify: Shoulder pinching: stop at about 60-70 degrees from the body.
Ribs uncomfortable on the pad: put a folded towel under the side.

muscleNotes.lat_deltoid_r: Prime mover: abducts the arm; the incline makes the lower part of the range harder than in a standing raise.
muscleNotes.ant_deltoid_r: Assists when the arm drifts forward.
muscleNotes.upper_traps_r: Upwardly rotates the shoulder blade near the top.
muscleNotes.infraspinatus_r: Holds the arm in a neutral rotation.
muscleNotes.obliques_r: Hold the trunk side-on against the pad.
muscleNotes.obliques_l: Hold the trunk side-on against the pad.
muscleNotes.glute_med_r: Steadies the hips on the staggered feet.
muscleNotes.glute_med_l: Steadies the hips on the staggered feet.

phases.label: Side-on to the pad, arm down
